extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and institutional applicants preparing a full application for the DOD FY24 Peer Reviewed Cancer Research Program (PRCRP) Idea Award
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare and submit a full application for the DoD FY24 PRCRP Peer Reviewed Cancer Idea Award, meeting all component, formatting, administrative, and review-related requirements described in the program announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full Application Submission Portal (extramural vs intramural)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extramural Submissions: Full applications from extramural organizations must be submitted through Grants.gov Workspace. Full applications from extramural organizations, including non-DOD federal organizations, received through eBRAP will be withdrawn. Intramural Submissions: Intramural DOD organizations may submit full applications through either eBRAP or Grants.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no CDMRP preference between portals for intramural submissions; intramural DOD organizations that choose Grants.gov should follow Extramural instructions; those unable to use Grants.gov should submit through eBRAP. Submission through the incorrect portal (e.g., extramural via eBRAP) will result in withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete full application package required
rubrics_metrics.description: Each application submission must include the completed full application package for this program announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Section II.H.3 checklist of required application components; each attachment must be uploaded as an individual file in the specified format and follow formatting guidelines in General Application Instructions, Appendix 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment 1: Project Narrative (six-page limit) — required content
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Narrative (six-page limit) must describe the proposed project using the specified outline: Hypothesis or Objective; Rationale; Specific Aims; Relevance to the Idea Award Intent; Research Strategy (experimental design, methods, analyses, controls); inclusion of human subjects/animals/statistics; strategy for inclusion of women and minorities, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page limit applies to text and non-text elements (figures, tables, graphs, photographs, diagrams, chemical structures, drawings). Inclusion of URLs that expand the Project Narrative is prohibited and may result in administrative withdrawal. Preliminary data is discouraged. This award may not be used to fund or conduct clinical trials. If human subjects/samples are used, include recruitment plan and document PI/collaborator experience. Describe potential problems/pitfalls and alternatives and, if applicable, statistical/power analyses and availability of tissue/data/human subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment 2: Supporting Documentation — allowed contents & restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine supporting documents into a single file named 'Support.pdf'. Start each document on a new page. Supporting Documentation should not include additional figures/tables/graphs/photographs/diagrams/chemical structures/drawings (these belong in the Project Narrative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed items include: References Cited; List of Abbreviations/Acronyms/Symbols; Facilities/Existing Equipment/Other Resources (no specific form); Publications and/or Patents (include URLs or up to five published manuscripts as PDF copies if not publicly available — extra items not reviewed); Letters of Organizational Support; Letters of Collaboration (signed); Intellectual and Material Property Plan (if applicable); Commercialization Strategy (if applicable); DOD Data Management Plan (two-page limit); Data and Research Resources Sharing Plan; Letters for Use of DOD/VA Resources (if applicable); anticipated inclusion enrollment tables for women/minorities (if applicable). Inclusion of items not requested or viewed as an extension of the Project Narrative may be removed or cause administrative withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment 3: Technical Abstract (one-page limit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload as 'TechAbs.pdf'. Technical abstract is used by all reviewers and will be posted publicly. Use only characters available on a standard QWERTY keyboard. Spell out Greek letters and other non-English letters/symbols. Graphics are not allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical abstract outline: Background (FY24 PRCRP Topic Area(s)), Objective/Hypothesis, Specific Aims, Study Design, Innovation, Impact (state FY24 PRCRP Overarching Challenge(s) and describe impact), Relevance to Military Health (identify Military Health Focus Area(s) and relevance to Service Members/Veterans/beneficiaries). Clarity and completeness within space limits are highly important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment 4: Lay Abstract (one-page limit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload as 'LayAbs.pdf'. Lay abstract addresses issues of particular interest to the affected community, is used by all reviewers, will be posted publicly, and must not duplicate the technical abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write for readers without a background in science/medicine; avoid jargon, acronyms, abbreviations. Address: FY24 PRCRP Topic Area(s); scientific objective and rationale in lay language; impact on patients (types helped, how, clinical applications, benefits/risks); FY24 PRCRP Overarching Challenge(s) and how research will make an impact; FY24 PRCRP Military Health Focus Area(s) and relevance to Service Members/Veterans/beneficiaries. Use only characters on standard QWERTY keyboard; spell out Greek/non-English letters; graphics not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment 5: Statement of Work (three-page limit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload as 'SOW.pdf'. Use the suggested SOW format available on eBRAP and refer to 'Example: Assembling a Generic Statement of Work' for guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the eBRAP 'Suggested SOW Format' and recommended strategies for assembling the SOW; submit as PDF. Page limit applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment 6: Relevance to Military Health Statement (one-page limit) — programmatic-only evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload as 'MilHealth.pdf'. Will be evaluated by the FY24 PRCRP Programmatic Panel during programmatic review only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the FY24 PRCRP Military Health Focus Area(s). Articulate relevance based on published literature of cancer impact on military populations and how the research will decrease the burden of cancer on Service Members, their Families, and Veterans. Identify environmental/occupational risk factors associated with Topic Area(s) and their short-/long-term impact on health/welfare/psychosocial wellness; or identify how the proposed research will support mission readiness by filling gaps in prevention/diagnosis/prognosis/treatment/quality of life/survivorship that profoundly impact Service Members/Families/Veterans. Articulate anticipated short-/long-term outcomes and potential impact on basic health/welfare/psychosocial wellness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment 7: Innovation Statement (one-page limit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload as 'Innovation.pdf'. Describe how the proposed research is innovative and not a fully developed laboratory research avenue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how the research may introduce a new paradigm, challenge existing paradigms, look at problems from new perspectives, or exhibit other highly creative qualities; demonstrate how proposed research is more than an incremental advance beyond ongoing research and published data; describe how it demonstrates innovative avenues. Page-limited to one page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment 8: Impact Statement (one-page limit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload as 'Impact.pdf'. Written in plain language for lay persons; state how the proposed work addresses a critical problem in at least one FY24 PRCRP Topic Area and how it will make an impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relate relevance of research to patient outcomes and how it benefits those affected by cancer. Describe pathway from proposed research (even if basic) to impact on cancer research and/or patient outcomes and how specific research goals fit into that pathway. Use plain language for lay people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment 9: Required Representations (extramural submissions only)
rubrics_metrics.description: All extramural applicants must complete and submit the Required Representations template available on eBRAP as 'RequiredReps.pdf'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For more information, see the General Application Instructions, Appendix 8, Section B, Representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment 10: Suggested Intragovernmental/Intramural Budget Form (if applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload as 'IGBudget.pdf' if an intramural DOD organization will be a collaborator. Complete a separate intragovernmental/intramural budget for each intramural DOD site covering the entire period of performance and include a budget justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include total costs per year for each subaward (direct and indirect) on the Grants.gov Research & Related Budget Form under subaward costs. Refer to General Application Instructions, Section V.A.(e) for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketches and Current/Previous/Pending Support (PI and key personnel)
rubrics_metrics.description: PI Biographical Sketch (five-page limit) and PI Previous/Current/Pending Support (no page limit). Key Personnel Biographical Sketches (five-page limit each) and Key Personnel Previous/Current/Pending Support (no page limit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload Biosketch files using naming convention 'Biosketch_LastName.pdf' and Support files as 'Support_LastName.pdf'. Information in biosketches will be used to evaluate personnel as part of unscored criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding restrictions: period, direct cost cap, allowable/disallowable costs, and indirect costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum period of performance is 2 years. The application's direct costs budgeted for the entire period of performance should not exceed $400,000. If indirect cost rates have been negotiated, indirect costs are to be budgeted in accordance with the organization’s negotiated rate. All direct and indirect costs of any subaward or contract must be included in the direct costs of the primary award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may request the entire maximum amount for projects with period less than 2 years. Direct costs may be requested for (not all-inclusive): travel in support of multidisciplinary collaborations and costs for one investigator to travel to one scientific/technical meeting per year to present project information or disseminate project results. Must not request clinical trial costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and attachment file rules (including prohibition on URLs in Project Narrative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each attachment must be uploaded as an individual file in the specified format and in accordance with formatting guidelines in the General Application Instructions, Appendix 2. The Project Narrative page limit applies to text and non-text elements. Inclusion of URLs that provide additional information that expands the Project Narrative and could confer an unfair competitive advantage is prohibited and may result in administrative withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to General Application Instructions Appendix 2 for detailed formatting. Supporting Documentation should not include figures/graphics (these belong in Project Narrative). Technical and Lay abstracts: use only QWERTY characters, spell out Greek letters, no graphics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant verification of full application submission in eBRAP
rubrics_metrics.description: After submission, files are transmitted to eBRAP; PI and organizational representatives receive an email instructing them to log into eBRAP to review, modify, and verify the full application submission. Verification is strongly recommended but not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eBRAP validates full application files against program requirements and notes discrepancies in the 'Full Application Files' tab but does not confirm file content accuracy. The Project Narrative and Research & Related Budget Form cannot be changed after the application submission deadline; if they fail validation or need modification, an updated full application must be submitted prior to the deadline. Other components (including subaward budgets and justifications) may be changed until the end of the application verification period. The full application cannot be modified once the verification period ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and SAM registration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant organization must be registered as an entity in SAM and have an 'Active' status before submitting via Grants.gov. Organizations must include the UEI generated by SAM in applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure SAM registration is active in time for submission; federal systems will be checked during award considerations as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission dates, times, and no-grace policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Start pre-application and application submission early to avoid missing deadlines. There are no grace periods. Failure to meet deadlines will result in submission rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All submission dates and times are indicated in Section I, Overview of the Funding Opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review—Scored Criterion: Scientific Merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific Merit is a scored criterion. Reviewers will assess: how well the proposed research addresses an important problem relevant to at least one FY24 PRCRP Topic Area; how well rationale, experimental design, and methodology (including appropriate controls) support the hypothesis; degree application articulates potential to generate robust preliminary data; whether any presented preliminary data indicates maturity beyond early research; appropriateness of statistical analysis plan (including power analysis if applicable); acknowledgment of potential problems and alternatives; demonstration of availability of tissue/data/human subjects if applicable; appropriateness and access to human subject population if applicable; appropriateness and robustness of experimental design for animal research if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These subpoints are considered together to determine technical merit; preliminary data is discouraged but if presented reviewers will judge whether it supports early investigation or demonstrates over-maturation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review—Scored Criterion: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovation is a scored criterion. Reviewers will assess: degree to which proposed research is innovative; whether it introduces new paradigms, challenges existing paradigms, interrogates problems from new perspectives, or exhibits other highly creative qualities; whether the proposed project studies a new area of research for the laboratory; extent to which the research represents more than an incremental advance beyond ongoing research and published data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Innovation is weighted equally with Scientific Merit and Impact in scored review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review—Scored Criterion: Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Impact is a scored criterion. Reviewers will assess: whether the application states explicitly how the proposed work addresses a critical problem in at least one FY24 PRCRP Topic Area; whether the application selects an FY24 PRCRP Overarching Challenge(s) and describes how the study will make an impact; whether the application articulates how the proposed research, even if basic, has a pathway toward making an impact on cancer research and/or patient outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impact must relate to FY24 PRCRP Overarching Challenges and show a pathway to patient outcomes; basic research must be connected to applicability to patients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review—Unscored Criteria: Personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel is an unscored criterion contributing to overall evaluation: based on biosketches, reviewers will assess to what degree the research team's background and experience are appropriate to accomplish the proposed research and how appropriate are the levels of effort proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considerations include PI and team qualifications, effort allocation, and documented experience (e.g., recruiting human subjects).

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review—Unscored Criteria: Budget
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget is an unscored criterion: reviewers will consider whether direct costs exceed allowable limits, whether the budget is appropriate for the proposed research, and whether there may be significant overlap with existing or pending awards of the PI or research team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceeding direct cost caps or significant overlap with other awards may negatively impact programmatic decisions; include accurate budget justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review—Unscored Criteria: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Environment is an unscored criterion: reviewers will assess whether the scientific environment is appropriate for the proposed research; whether requirements are supported by availability/accessibility to facilities and resources (including collaborations); quality and extent of institutional support; and, if applicable, whether the intellectual and material property plan is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide Facilities/Equipment/Other Resources descriptions and letters of organizational support when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review—Unscored Criteria: Application Presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Application Presentation is an unscored criterion: reviewers will consider the influence of writing, clarity, and presentation of application components on the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity and organization of Project Narrative, Abstracts, and attachments can affect review; poor presentation may reduce reviewers' ability to judge merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic Review criteria (used for funding recommendations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Programmatic reviewers use: ratings and evaluations of peer reviewers and relevance to DHP and FY24 PRCRP priorities as evidenced by adherence to the intent of the award mechanism; program portfolio composition; programmatic relevance to FY24 PRCRP Military Health Focus Area(s); programmatic relevance to FY24 PRCRP Overarching Challenge(s); and relative innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programmatic review is comparison-based and selects application(s) that best achieve program objectives; highest peer-scored applications are not automatically funded. Relevance to program priorities and portfolio balance can outweigh peer scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-tier review process and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications are evaluated in a two-tier review: first tier is peer review to determine technical merit against established criteria; second tier is programmatic review for programmatic relevance. All CDMRP review processes are conducted confidentially; panel members sign confidentiality statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personnel at applicant/collaborating organizations are prohibited from contacting reviewers or persons involved in the review/approval process; violations will result in administrative withdrawal and possible suspension/debarment. Unauthorized disclosure of confidential information is a crime (18 USC 1905).

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity and performance information (SAM review prior to award)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to making an assistance agreement award where federal share exceeds the simplified acquisition threshold, the federal awarding agency will review and consider any information about the applicant available in SAM. Applicants may review SAM and submit comments on any information entered previously by a federal awarding agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal awarding agency will consider applicant comments and other information in the designated integrity and performance system when determining recipient qualifications according to DoDGARs Section 22.415.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award administration: notices, negotiation, and obligating authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Each applicant and PI will receive email notification when funding recommendations are posted to eBRAP and a peer review summary statement. If recommended for funding, a government representative will contact the person authorized to negotiate on behalf of the recipient organization. Only an appointed USAMRAA Grants Officer may obligate the government to expend funds; no commitment should be inferred from other discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intra-DOD obligations will be made according to negotiated Inter-Agency Agreements and managed by a CDMRP Science Officer. Intragovernmental and intramural DOD investigators must coordinate receipt/commitment of funds through their Resource Manager/Comptroller.

rubrics_metrics.name: PI changes and award transfers restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes in PI are not allowed except under extenuating circumstances evaluated case-by-case. Organizational transfer of an award will not be allowed in the last year of the original period of performance or any extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to General Application Instructions, Appendix 7, Section F, for information on organization or PI changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative and national policy requirements and terms/conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicable requirements in the DoDGARs (32 CFR) and 2 CFR apply to resulting grants/cooperative agreements. Refer to General Application Instructions Appendix 7 and Appendix 8 for administrative and national policy requirements. Refer to latest DoD R&D Terms and Conditions and USAMRAA Research Terms and Conditions addendum for further information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure compliance with referenced federal regulations and award terms if recommended for funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human and animal subjects compliance prior to implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications recommended for funding that involve animals, human data, human specimens, human subjects, or human cadavers must be reviewed for compliance with federal and DOD animal and/or human subjects protection requirements and approved by the USAMRDC Office of Human and Animal Research Oversight prior to implementation. This is in addition to local IACUC/IRB/Ethics Committee review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to General Application Instructions, Appendix 6, for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirements and Award Expiration Transition Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual technical progress reports and a final technical progress report are required, prepared in accordance with the Research Performance Progress Report. An Award Expiration Transition Plan must be submitted with the final progress report (one-page template available on eBRAP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Award Expiration Transition Plan must outline whether/how the research supported by the award will progress and include known or pending sources of funding. Award Terms/Conditions will specify whether additional/more frequent reporting is required. Recipients with cumulative federal awards >$10M must disclose certain legal proceedings to SAM semiannually per Representations requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-submission validation and modification windows
rubrics_metrics.description: eBRAP will validate full application files and note discrepancies; applicants are responsible for reviewing components and ensuring proper ordering. The Project Narrative and Research & Related Budget Form cannot be changed after the application submission deadline; other components may be changed until the end of the application verification period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Project Narrative or budget fail eBRAP validation or need modification, an updated full application must be submitted prior to the deadline. The full application cannot be modified once the verification period ends.
